messages:
maria: Quick follow-up from the console auth bridge RFC — we need a concrete post-cutover plan for rolling the proxy out and how we'll measure any RBAC-induced latency regressions. TL;DR: rolling canary + observability hooks + fallback path.

jon: +1. Can you sketch the canary criteria? e.g., p50/p95 token-check latency, error rate, and dashboard rendering time delta?

maria: Thinking: p50 token-check under 8ms, p95 under 40ms, auth error rate <0.1%, and dashboard render pipeline end-to-end increase <5% for canary cohort. If any threshold trips -> auto rollback. Thoughts?

sam: Those look reasonable. Two practical concerns: (1) where do we inject the bridge in the query path without duplicating KV lookups? (2) how do we avoid double counting when caching prefixes across the bridge?

kevin: For (1) we should place the delegate proxy between the request router and the authz adapter so the router still does tenant routing but the proxy owns token exchange. That avoids touching the per-panel fetch logic.

tara: For (2) caching: proxy should expose a cache key rewrite rule. If cache is based on (user, tenant, query-hash) we add a proxy-version suffix so old cache entries remain valid until TTL expires. That prevents sudden cache invalidation across rollout.

jon: I want an explicit migration step: stage A (proxy reads, no-writes), stage B (proxy reads+writes with shadow traffic), stage C (proxy authoritative). Each stage should be gated by canary success and automated smoke tests.

maria: Agreed. We'll also need a low-latency fallback: if the proxy doesn't respond within 120ms, router should short-circuit to existing auth path (with a metric tag so we can count fallbacks). ops-bot: please create alert when fallback >0.5% of requests for 10m.

ops-bot: Alert created: channel=#eng-oncall, query=rate(fallback_proxy[10m]) > 0.005 -> severity=high.

kevin: Implementation note: keep the proxy stateless and push session caching to a shared LRU with a 5k entry default. That keeps failover cheap. Also expose /metrics with histograms for token-check latency.

sam: Agree on statelessness. One addition: for long queries we should stream auth checks so the UI isn't blocked by sequential auth-verification across N panels. Approach: return immediate 202 + optimistic render, then patch-in panels as auth checks complete. UX will be slightly different but faster.

tara: UX tradeoff: optimistic render may show placeholders for some panels. Product ok with that? @maria

maria: We can ship optimistic render only for low-sensitivity dashboards (flagged in metadata). For sensitive dashboards keep blocking mode. We'll maintain a dashboard metadata field: "auth_render_mode": "blocking|optimistic".

jon: That implies the query layer needs to check per-dashboard metadata quickly. We should cache metadata in the proxy with TTL 30s and invalidate on dashboard edits.

kevin: Sample config for proxy cache policy:

```
cache:
  ttl_seconds: 30
  max_entries: 5000
  key_template: "dashboard_v1:{dashboard_id}:{proxy_version}"
```

sam: Looks good. One more perf note: measuring end-to-end dashboard latency needs synthetic probes that hit representative multi-panel dashboards. We'll add a canary suite with 5 dashboard shapes (1-panel, 3-panel, 8-panel, heavy-embed, search-heavy).

maria: Who owns the probes? @jon @eng-sre

jon: Eng-platform will own probe definitions. Eng-sre will own alert thresholds and on-call runbook.

ops-bot: Runbook created: doc link -> https://internal.redwood/prod/console/auth-bridge-cutover-runbook (placeholder)

tara: Security ask: audit logs must include pre/post proxy auth decision, minimal PII, and a trace_id. We'll need a protobuf change to the auth event schema.

kevin: Proto change should be additive: add auth_event.v2 with fields: trace_id, decision, auth_provider, latency_ms_bucket. Keep v1 for compatibility.

sam: Migration plan for proto: proxy emits v2; consumers can read v1 fields if present. We'll run a traffic shadow to ensure downstream can parse v2.

maria: OK action list:
- jon: define canary cohorts + synthetic probes (due EOD Thu)
- kevin: implement proxy with /metrics and cache (PR by Mon)
- sam: add optimistic rendering flow + dashboard metadata flag (spike Fri)
- tara: spec audit log proto change + compliance review (next Tue)
- ops-bot: create alerts and runbook (done/linked)

jon: One last question: can we quantify cost delta? Proxy introduces additional token checks ~0.5-1k QPS in peak -> estimate cost increase ~0.8% CPU and 2% mem/egress. Finance okay with small bump if it stabilizes latency.

maria: I'll ping finance. If anyone hits a canary trip, post the trace_id here and we'll triage. Thanks all :thumbsup:
